text: I can make room for an extra step or two on each side if that's what it takes to keep her steady, but I can't have it lined with anything she might catch a hoof on. If she needs space, what about the surface? Can she walk on something that isn't smooth, so I'm less likely to slip around?

text: The weight I carry every day is tough enough; if whatever we have to cross adds more strain, I'll be worn out before noon. What are you dealing with on the other side?

text: What I carry is longer than I am by three or four times, and it doesn't bend — so a straight run is everything to me, and room at both ends to swing the end round without clouting somebody. text: It's the uneven footing that does me in — I can handle the length if there's a solid surface beneath me. If you're swinging those long pieces around, should we aim for something wide enough to give you space to maneuver?

speaker: role2

text: My hands ache from the weight, and dropping into the water would ruin all of it for the day.

text: Then we want the same thing from it, near enough — you can't have it give under your hands, and she won't set a hoof on anything that shifts a hair under her. She feels it before I do; if it breathes even once she'll plant and back off, and then neither of us gets across today.
